$comment: P0-06 — the certified main-branch protection contract for the Bizosto marketing website.
This is the website half of the certification whose ERP half lives in
lacreativodesign/nextjs-boilerplate. The two are deliberately SEPARATE files verified by
SEPARATE workflows, each running inside the repository it certifies, under that
repository's own job token.
That separation is the point. This repository is PRIVATE, and a job token issued to the
ERP repository cannot read it — GitHub answers 404. A cross-repository read that fails
must never be reported as a successful certification, so neither repository vouches for
the other.
It holds no credential.
Same gap, same single account, same reason as the ERP entry above. The two
repositories share one owner, so supplying a reviewer for one does not supply one
for the other - each needs its own collaborator added before its count can go to 1.
The ONLY check this repository produces. It has no .github directory at all, so
there are no GitHub Actions workflows and no check runs - `Vercel` arrives as a
commit STATUS, and it was success on main at 83ae0648.
Requiring anything else here would block every merge forever. Integration id 8329
is the Vercel app: the same id is pinned on the ERP repository, where PR #1011
reached mergeable_state 'clean' with it, which is what proves the id is right for
this owner's Vercel integration rather than merely plausible.
NOT YET APPLIED, AND THE REASON MATTERS.
This repository MUST REMAIN PRIVATE. It holds proprietary Bizosto marketing source.
GitHub Free serves rulesets on public repositories only; Pro, Team and Enterprise
serve them on private repositories too. So on the current plan a private
bizosto-website cannot carry a ruleset at all, and the API says so:
403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public to enable this feature."
That error names two ways out and only ONE of them is acceptable. The correct owner
action is to UPGRADE THE ACCOUNT to GitHub Pro or higher. Publishing proprietary
source to obtain a security control is not a remedy, it is a larger exposure than the
one it closes, and P0-06 rejects it.
On 2026-09-17 the repository was briefly made public in an attempt to unblock this.
That was a policy violation, it is being reverted to private, and it is recorded here
rather than erased. `expectedVisibility` is now a checked control precisely so that a
repeat reads as DRIFT rather than as progress: see ruleset.visibility in the verifier.
Because the repository is private, the ERP repository's job-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN cannot
read it. Its ruleset is therefore verified by a companion workflow running INSIDE
bizosto-website under its own job token, not from here. A cross-repository read that
fails must never be reported as a successful certification.
